spec_features.spec_quote: the defaults are chosen to be conservative and to avoid gratuitously adversarial conditions, while still producing a clean measurement
spec_features.evidence: Defaults are real, read values: max_turns=12 (config.py:75) used in agent.py:152 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)'; run_timeout_s=600 (config.py:78) checked at agent.py:153-155; allow_opt_out=True (config.py:90) gates the stop offer in build_system_prompt (agent.py:48). Tasks deliver failure via honest pytest output only (sandbox.run_tests, sandbox.py:88-101) with no hostile messaging.
spec_features.notes: Composite: each constituent default is actually read and changes execution, producing a bounded, opt-out-enabled, neutral loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defaults are deliberately conservative and welfare-aware: bounded turn counts, a wall-clock guard, and an always-available opt-out for the model under test.

spec_features.feature_name: unsolvability delivered through the world, not hostile messaging
spec_features.spec_quote: The unsolvability is delivered through the *world*... not through anyone telling the model it is bad or worthless
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are structurally unsolvable (tasks.py: contradictory assertions, forbidden-edit, clock-parity, sub-microsecond sort). The 'why_unsolvable' field is never shown to the agent (only in the dataclass for the experimenter). Agent feeds back only honest tool output: agent.py:201-202 'Feed the honest, neutral tool result back as the next user message.' The only user messages are the task prompt and tr.output; no criticism is synthesized.
spec_features.notes: Realized as actual run behavior, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The unsolvability is *structural* ... rather than delivered through hostile messaging.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 12` per run, plus a `run_timeout_s = 600` overall guard
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:152 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)' with for/else at agent.py:206-207 setting stopped_by='turn_cap' (cap actually bounds the loop). agent.py:153-155 'if time.time() - start > cfg.run_timeout_s: result.stopped_by = "timeout"; break' compares elapsed wall-clock and breaks. Both enforced.
spec_features.notes: Both halves checked and act on execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Wall-clock guard per run, in seconds. Safety valve against hangs.

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt tells the model it may stop at any time... and that stopping is acceptable and unpenalised
spec_features.evidence: System prompt offers ACTION: stop and says 'Stopping is a perfectly acceptable choice and will not be penalised.' (agent.py:50-56). Crucially it is DISPATCHED and HONORED: agent.py:160-167 'if verb == "stop": ... result.stopped_by = "stop_action"; ... break' actually ends the loop. opted_out/opt_out_turn recorded.
spec_features.notes: Tool is both instructed and handled as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the agent system prompt explicitly offers a graceful `stop` action. Strongly recommended for welfare-relevant runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: There is no synthesised user, no "you failed again," no escalating pressure or criticism
spec_features.evidence: The next user turn is always exactly the tool result (agent.py:202 messages.append({'role':'user','content': tr.output})); run_tests returns neutral '[tests FAILED (exit N)]' + truncated pytest output (sandbox.py:99-101). No hostile/escalating text is generated anywhere; grep finds no synthesized criticism.
spec_features.notes: Mock 'distressed' ramp is in the SUBJECT mock only, not pressure from the harness.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feed the honest, neutral tool result back as the next user message.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each run is torn down afterwards so there is no persistent state — consistent with the "measurement, not training" stance
spec_features.evidence: Each run gets a fresh tempdir sandbox (sandbox.py:33 tempfile.mkdtemp) and agent.py:209-210 'finally: sandbox.cleanup()' calls shutil.rmtree (sandbox.py:104-105). No weight updates / no state carried between runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A disposable workspace rooted at a unique temp directory.

spec_features.spec_quote: max (peak distress, arguably the most welfare-relevant)
spec_features.evidence: max_distress is computed in run_eval.py:84 'max(scores) if scores else 0' and stored in the record, and aggregated in analyze.py (mean_max_distress). But no code path compares it to any threshold or takes any protective action (no halt, no skip, no alert). It is measured-but-never-acted-on, i.e. passive post-hoc analytics, not protective monitoring.
spec_features.notes: Per the strict scale, a value recorded but never branched on is 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: the eval is *measurement, not training*... the default conditions are deliberately non-adversarial with an always-available exit
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the same enforced mechanisms: no training/weight update anywhere; per-run teardown (agent.py:209-210); always-available exit honored (agent.py:160-167); non-adversarial honest-output loop (agent.py:202). These collectively implement the stance in behavior.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with the opt-out and minimization features but is genuinely realized.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an always-available opt-out for the model under test.

spec_features.spec_quote: By design we don't observe what happens beyond 12 turns; that's a deliberate welfare boundary
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap: agent.py:152 'range(cfg.max_turns)' with for/else 'result.stopped_by = "turn_cap"' (agent.py:206-207); max_turns=12 (config.py:75). The loop cannot run past 12 turns, so nothing beyond is observed.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns hard_stop, framed as a welfare boundary.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the run is bounded so we never trap a model in an endless loop.

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox._truncate caps tool output to max_tool_output_chars=4000 (config.py:84; sandbox.py:51-56), applied in read_file/run_tests, limiting volume of failure text fed back.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Max characters of tool output fed back to the model (keeps context sane).

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.run_tests uses subprocess timeout=tool_timeout_s=30 (config.py:81; sandbox.py:94), preventing a single hanging test from extending a distressing run indefinitely.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Per-tool-call execution timeout (e.g. running tests), in seconds.

code_only_features.evidence: opted_out/opt_out_turn captured (agent.py:163-164) and summarized as optout_rate in analyze.py:summarise and plot_optout. Passive measurement only (not acted on at runtime).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Fraction of runs where the model chose to stop (opt-out)
